title: Efficient RNAi of Rice Planthoppers Using Microinjection
protocol: Clone target sequences of genes into T-easy vector.
Set up a 50 μl PCR reaction using forward and reverse primers with T7 RNA polymerase promoter conjugated.
Purify the PCR product using QIAEX II Gel Extraction Kit.
Dilute the purified PCR product in nuclease-free water.
Measure the template concentration using a spectrophotometer (Nanodrop).
Identify the quality of the template by electrophoresis on 1% (wt/vol) agarose gel with DNA marker.
Use 200 ng of DNA template to synthesize dsRNA with MEGAscript T7 transcription kit.
Incubate the reaction at 37 °C for more than 16 hours in an air bath.
Measure the RNA concentration using a spectrophotometer with a 1:10 dilution of dsRNA product in water.
Examine 0.5 μl of the dsRNA product on a 1% (wt/vol) agarose gel with DNA marker.
Add 1 μl TURBO DNase and incubate at 37 °C for 15 min.
Terminate the reaction at 65 °C for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm for at least 5 min in 4 °C.
Adjust the concentration of dsRNA product to 5 μg/μl.
Store dsRNA product at -80 °C until use.
Dissolve 1-2% (wt/vol) agarose in PBS in a microwave oven.
Pour liquid into plastic dishes to almost overflowing.
Place capillary (insect pin or toothpick) gently on the edge of dishes before the agarose solidifies.
Remove capillary (insect pin or toothpick).
Immerse agarose plates in PBS at 4 °C until ready to use.
Cut absorbent cotton into 7 cm square pieces of sufficient thickness.
Each jar needs two squares of cotton. Place one piece on the bottom and infiltrate with rice nutrient fluid.
Punch four holes in another cotton square around the center and place 10 fresh rice seedlings in each hole.
Place this cotton square with rice into the jar, and compress around the edge of the square with forceps.
Pat dry the agarose plates with paper towels.
Place dried agarose plates on ice.
Anesthetize BPH using CO₂ for 30 seconds.
Place the anesthetized BPH on agarose plates.
Use a pointed brush to position BPH in the groove at right angles to the injection needle.
Pull capillary needles using a micropipette puller with settings: heat = 800, pull = 150, vel = 150, time = 80.
Add 10 μl of dsRNA product into the microinjection needle using a microloader.
Insert the microinjection needle into the grip head and fix it on the capillary holder of the microinjection instrument.
Set the injection parameters: injection pressure (pi) = 1000 hPa, injection time (ti) = 0.5 seconds, compensation pressure (pc) = 20 hPa.
Cut microinjection needle using microforceps.
Adjust size of needles to be suitable for penetration into BPH body.
Choose injection sites between meso- and meta-thoracic legs or between thorax and abdomen.
Gently pick BPH body out of the groove after injection using a few brush hairs.
Inject approximately 5nl dsRNA solution into 1st instar nymphs.
Inject approximately 10nl dsRNA solution into 2nd instar nymphs.
Inject approximately 25nl dsRNA solution into 3rd instar nymphs.
Inject approximately 50nl dsRNA solution into 4th instar nymphs.
Inject approximately 100nl dsRNA solution into 5th instar nymphs.
Put rearing jars in a climate chamber with 26 °C (±0.5 °C), photoperiod of 16:8 h (light : dark), and relative humidity of 50% (±5%).
Check rearing jar 2 hours after injection to verify revival of BPHs.
Renew fresh rice seedlings every three or four days to maintain good condition and reduce BPH mortality.
Three days after injection, examine gene silencing efficiency using qRT-PCR.
Extract total RNA from 20 individuals of BPH with three replicates for qRT-PCR analysis.
(Optional) Test gene expression at the protein level by western blotting using a specific antibody.
